purpose: Builds the tree of a project's levels (Business, Product, Solution and any the project added) for a level chooser, and gives a card the one hook that reads them and adds a level, with the host doing every read and write.
namedChanges: `const VEDA = "https://veda.gilb.com/base/t"` (line 31) is removed, and the `ontologyTerm` of each entry of `DEFAULT_LEVELS` (lines 39-42) is a getter. The source evaluated `DEFAULT_LEVELS` when the module loaded, before an app can set the term origin, so each entry is now `get ontologyTerm() { return `${termOrigin()}/base/t/BusinessLevel`; }` (and the same with `StakeholderLevel`, `ProductLevel`, `SolutionLevel`, the names of the source's literals). Read after `setTermOrigin` with the app's origin, it gives the string the source had. `termOrigin` is `@kaigilb/gilbplatformcode-term-origin`.

`useQueryClient()` (line 480) is `useContext(ProjectLevelsHostContext)`, throwing an error that names the provider when there is none. `useAllLevels(vaultId)` (line 481) is `host.useAllLevels(vaultId)` (host member 1). `waitForLevels(qc, vaultId)` (lines 487 and 492) is `host.waitForLevels(vaultId)` (member 2). `ensureDefaultLevels(vaultId, qc)` (line 488) is `host.ensureDefaultLevels(vaultId)` (member 3). `addProjectLevel(vaultId, qc, label, parentToken)` (line 493) is `host.addProjectLevel(vaultId, label, parentToken)` (member 4). In the two dependency arrays `qc` is `host`. The calls are in the source's places and order.
`directChildren` (line 398) and `nextPosition` (line 411), private in the source, are exported, so a host can write `addProjectLevel` with them.

library.title: Project levels (Business, Product, Solution)
library.note: Reads and adds a project's levels for the level chooser; the line that shows them is plan-type-level-version.
